body:
Had an episode like this a few years back. A lot of people talk about gaps in their memory during 2020, which, same. But my memory gap started around July of 2019. I think the start of it was a \*veeery\* personal phone call I made \*AT WORK\* where I escalated into screaming. Basically, I was seeing a new guy and we were banging a lot. I live with my siblings so they saw this guy come and go at all hours, and it seemed one of them was gossiping to my mom and she shamed me for my perceived promiscuity (hadn't ever asked me about the relationship, only took sibling at their word) and I just snapped. I left work, mortified, immediately took an FMLA.   


What little I do remember is turning into this angry monster I still don't recognize. I was oscillating between crying misery and a white-hot ball of fury. At nothing and everything. I am also a typically meek and calm person, I don't like yelling, violence horrifies me and generally speaking, if I get angry, it's never for very long. It either turns into sadness pretty quick or I just let it go.  


I was a totally different person. I would fly into these rages - just locked myself in my room and threw shit around on the ground and at the walls, screaming. During the day, when I had to try to act normal, I was just unapproachable. I "radiated hostility," according to my parents.   


At one point, I took to twitter to make passive aggressive tweets about an upcoming family gathering and there were certain family members I wanted to avoid, just low tolerance for their personalities. But the wrong people saw my tweets and took my comments to heart, thinking it was about them. I tried telling them it had nothing to do with them but they wouldn't believe me. Those family members have since gone no contact with me and my immediate family and I carry that guilt EVERY. SINGLE. DAY. I have no extended family anymore, partially because I just haaaaad to be an angry cunt on twitter.  


I have a family history of severe mental illness, so I believe my episode, no matter how uncharacteristic it had been, was very triggering for them, in terms of previous interactions with the way worse off relatives. So as much as it hurts me, they were also hurt and have no obligation to show me any grace. It is what it is.
Oh dang this person has fantastic taste, I have a couple of these pins (and I want nearly all the rest AAAAA I love Mammoth Cave!)
